content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days.
- Overestimates prices after sharp spikes (e.g., post-80.00+), often overshooting by 5–10% and failing to correct quickly.
- Shows persistent downward bias in the latter half of the forecast (last 10–15 days), suggesting mean reversion is not captured.
- Lags in response to recent price increases — model reacts slowly to upward momentum, especially after 75–80 range.
- Tends to overcorrect after minor declines, creating artificial volatility in the middle of the forecast.
- Underestimates the impact of recent high prices (e.g., 80+), failing to reflect sustained premium or policy-driven support.
- Sensitive to initial conditions — forecasts are more inaccurate when history includes recent sharp drops or volatility.
